design.closed_form: x_l = M_l^+ d*_l ; q = sum_l d*_l' x_l ; u = b x / sqrt(q); M_l = Gram of unit W_down columns
design.d_star_j2: teacher-forced J2 gradient on the fixed prompt prefix (incumbent, plan 2.40/2.42)
design.d_star_pw: pathwise term E_y[grad_u phi_path(y)], phi_path = path J2 in nats (plan 2.42)

C0_gram.fact: M_l = Wn' Wn with Wn 2560x9216 has rank 2560 < 9216, so the FULL Gram is SINGULAR: Cholesky fails at leading minor 2559. Only 32-coordinate principal blocks are PD, which is why every committed result lives on a small support.
C0_gram.consequence: the physical budget does not charge 6656 directions per layer; the number of distinguishable injection directions per layer is 2560, not 9216. The min-norm (M^+) solution is the parameter-free choice.

SELF.note: budget tolerance relaxed to 1e-2: u carries components along singular values down to 1e-6*max, so the quadratic form inherits ~1e-3 fp32 error

A.consistency: this reproduces the gradient-level cos 0.4187 of plan 2.42 after the metric - the two independent measurements of 'what swapping d* does' agree

verdict: Swapping d* rotates the budget-optimal direction by cos_M 0.4306 and replaces 38 of the top-64 positions (Jaccard 0.255). On the teacher-forced readout the incumbent wins by 2.25x at b=0.05 and 2.18x at b=0.10 - which is EXPECTED, since d*_j2 is by construction the gradient of exactly that readout under exactly that metric. So this experiment CANNOT adjudicate which d* is right: each is optimal for its own functional. The only adjudicator is behaviour, and the gradient route to it is closed (plan 2.42, r(32)=0.022).
what_follows: The behaviour arm must be measured directly and paired (u_j2 vs u_pw at fixed b), not inferred from gradients. That is the C2 gate, and it is the only remaining knob-free question.
